tweets.text:
Details of the Bunni protocol attack from this week.

Bunni is one of the first Uniswap v4 hook-based protocols. 

"The exploit was enabled by a precision error in Bunni’s Liquidity Distribution Function (LDF) during swap rebalancing. When swaps passes through Uniswap v4,  the hook logic miscalculated balance deltas, leaving small amounts  unaccounted for. Instead of offsetting, these errors accumulated as a  net credit to the attacker."

I would go even deeper into the root cause. Smart contracts are designed to manage money. To manage money, you need very solid math primitives and special language support for these, so that it is impossible or very difficult to get these kinds of issues wrong. In this case, it's lack of Solidity's built in support for advanced math that is an issue. 

Now, it feels a bit like Solidity developers need to work on too low-level math primitives. Because Solidity itself does not have functionality to reason about math calculations, it is 1) hard to write math 2) hard to reason about math code 3) difficult to auto detect mistakes made with math. Wads, mulDivs(), different fixed point accuracy conversions are all the symptoms of the same problem.

https://t.co/HWIeyEy3VA

By @quillaudits_ai

tweets.text:
Earlier I said I’d wait for the full breakdown of the @bunni_xyz exploit.

Here it is.

Bunni V2, built on Uniswap v4, lost over $8M after a precision bug in its liquidity accounting. The Liquidity Distribution Function (LDF) was exploited.

Bunni introduces its own liquidity curve on top of @Uniswap v4.

After every trade, the system checks if the curve shifted and rebalances the pool to maintain the right ratios.

The flaw was in how post-swap balances were calculated.

A precision error allowed small miscalculations to slip through.

By executing swaps of very specific sizes, the attacker was able to trigger these miscalculations repeatedly.

Instead of canceling out, the errors accumulated into a net credit.

Once large enough, they were able to withdraw more tokens than their swaps should have allowed.

On Ethereum, they took a 3M USDT flash loan from Uniswap v3 and ran a series of controlled swaps on the USDC/USDT pool through Uniswap v4’s PoolManager.

Each swap triggered Bunni’s hook and compounded the imbalance.

Eventually, they withdrew the inflated USDC/USDT, repaid the flash loan, and deposited the stolen funds into @aave.

On Unichain, they used a 2000 WETH flash loan from @MorphoLabs, extracted 1366 WETH with the same strategy, and bridged it back to Ethereum through @AcrossProtocol.

In total, $8.3M was drained.

A subtle precision error in a custom liquidity mechanism, amplified by flash loans and repeated swaps was all it took.

The Bunni protocol, built on Uniswap v4, lost ~$8.4M in September to a logic bug and got shutdown yesterday. It wasn’t the core AMM fault, it was a custom hook doing the damage.

Think hook = mini-contract.

Every hook needs its own threat model:

• Re-entrancy,
• Rounding bias,
• Gas DoS,
• Cross-pool state, etc.

Version 4 lifts the base layer, but you inherit all the risk.

For projects building on Uniswap v4, please get your hook logic reviewed now, not after the funds vanish.

And FYI; QuillAudits playbook for Uniswap v4 includes:

1⃣ Precision/fuzz testing of liquidity flows.
2⃣ Withdrawal-path proofs.
3⃣ Invariants in custom LDF logic.
4⃣ Fee Models.
5⃣ Reward Distribution.

Utilise the free community good to your advantage.

If you skip these, you’re exposed. 👇👇

Hello everyone, it is with saddened hearts that we announce the shutdown of Bunni.

The recent exploit has forced Bunni's growth to a halt, and in order to securely relaunch we'd need to pay 6-7 figures in audit & monitoring expenses alone – requiring capital that we simply don't have. It'd also take months of development & BD effort just to get Bunni back to where it was before the exploit, which we cannot afford. Thus, we have decided it's best to shut down Bunni.

Here's what will happen:
- Bunni users will still be able to withdraw assets via the Bunni website until further notice.
- We intend to distribute the remaining treasury assets to BUNNI, LIT, and veBUNNI holders based on a snapshot. However, the validation of the legal process is ongoing, and the exact details of the distribution will be shared at a later date once the legal process is finalized. Team members will be excluded from the snapshot.
- The Bunni v2 smart contracts have been relicensed from BUSL to MIT, enabling everyone to utilize our innovations such as LDFs, surge fees, and autonomous rebalancing. We have pushed the AMM space forward by a generation, and it would be a shame if our efforts went to waste.
- We will continue working with law enforcement to recover the stolen funds from the exploiter.

Thank you to everyone who has supported us throughout our journey to push DeFi forward.

tweets.text:
While searching for projects building on uni v4 (ETA Q4'24), I came across @bunni_xyz and it's perhaps the best thing i've seen in the last six months. If you have 60 seconds i'd like to share the idea with you, you got a minute?

Overview and Features
Quick recap - Uni v4 hooks will enable a "hook economy", transforming Uniswap into a valuable infra layer for dapps like Bunni to build on.

Bunni is a revolutionary AMM that introduces several features to optimise liquidity provision and maximise LP profits. Being one of the first-movers in this hook economy (since Q4'23), here are some high-level features you can expect:

1. Shapeshifting liquidity: LP in any shape (i.e. center-heavy, edge-heavy, etc) while being able to define conditions for automatic shifting (i.e. shift with TWAP price, volatility, etc)

2. Auto rebalancing: Autonomous management of ratios between two underlying tokens if liquidity shifts. This removes the need for automated liq managers (i.e. gamma/arrakis) or manual management.

3. Rehypothecation: A feature where idle assets are being put to work in external vaults (i.e. Aave/Gearbox), increasing returns to LPs.

4. Auction-Managed AMM (am-AMM): Where pool managers (decided via auction mechanism) obtain an edge to capture arb/MEV opportunities, as they can do so without incurring swap fees. They can also dynamically adjust fee parameters (i.e. directional swap fees, surge fees, etc) to maximise returns to LPs.

5. Gas-efficient swaps: The gas for swaps in bunni v2 remains constant regardless of the number of ticks crossed. This makes it highly efficient for power users.

Why it's important
As a result of toxic order flow (i.e. arb trades on passive LPs), research has shown that the average LP on uni v3 is unprofitable. On average, IL represents ~130% of the fees that pools earn.

Source: https://t.co/Fcnj9EayiE

While these implementations may seem "non-essential" on its own, they all work together towards maximising profits for LPs and incentivising liquid onchain markets.

Bunni v2's Progress
- Building v2 since Q4'23 ✅
- Testnet live since July ✅
- Rehypothecation partnerships (Frax, Gearbox, Compound, Spark, Morpho, etc) ✅
- Uniswap X fillers 🕑
- Audit in progress 🕑
- Tokenomics revamp 🕑

Thesis for Bunni v2
1. Premier destination for sophisticated LPs: It makes economic sense for sophisticated LPs to use Bunni v2 as a tool to deploy liquidity on uni v4, as they get to enjoy higher yields (from rehypo) and potentially lower IL (from auto management and other features). This is also less resource-intensive from a pool management perspective.

The high degree of parameter customisation offers complete freedom for them to experiment with various strategies in accordance with their edge or market outlook.

2. Rehypothecation to attract TVL from collateral assets: Given that idle tokens on both sides can be rehypothecated for extra yields, I expect liquidity on major pairs to migrate to Bunni.

To put things into perspective, the addressable TVL  here is approximately $3.1b. Assumptions: Top 10 collateral assets on Aave v3 (ETH) being actively supplied as liquidity on DEXes.

3. Promotes experimentation: LDF and shapeshifting features may attract long-tailed assets and other novel experiments. Probably not the best example but think along the line of Jimbos/White Lotus-type of liquidity experiments.

4. Little/No direct competitors: I have yet to come across any project building something similar to bunni v2 on top of uni v4. We may see a handful emerge soon but we gotta remember that Rome wasn't built in a day - the team has been building v2 for close to a year now. What I'm trying to say here is - there is no other uni v4 proxy available on the market atm.

5. Risk-Reward favours the upside: Despite the recent proliferation of $AAVE, defi is still a relatively underowned sector this cycle and often thought of as contrarian. There are also macro-level catalysts with trump's candidacy being a barometer for future defi performance.

Past investors in $LIT are now fully vested and at $10m FDV, (i think) it is below their cost basis. Most observoors would scoff at the chart - down 90% from ATHs with terrible volume (< $70k in the past 24h). These factors do make 1 thing clear: $LIT is severely underowned and overlooked. With impending macro/micro level catalysts, a superior product, and tokenomics revamp, I am expecting $LIT to reprice aggressively once it captures broader market attention.

Concluding Thoughts
- Bunni v2 is a first-mover, building a differentiated and superior product
- The setup offers asymmetric upside: nobrainer valuation coupled with impending product launch/rebrand
- The TAM is pretty significant (> $3b)
- Bullish on the product x LP x tokenholder flywheel (see below)

That's all folks. As always, NFA and DYOR.
